source.title: Spectrum of inner-product kernel matrices in the polynomial regime and multiple descent phenomenon in kernel ridge regression

record.tranche_reason: The paper theoretically analyzes test-error curves for kernel ridge regression, a different model class from deep networks, and derives conditions for double and multiple descent.
record.gate_note: The paper's own asymptotic KRR test-error results are included. Its kernel-spectrum results do not themselves measure test error; descriptions of results from cited prior work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The paper derives, as its own theorem (Theorem 3, Eq. 19), the exact asymptotic test error of inner-product kernel ridge regression as n/B(Ad,ℓ)→ψ. The bias term falls in ψ and the variance term peaks at ψ=1, so the risk curve can double descend, and repeat at each integer κ. This is a different method (rigorous asymptotic theory) and model class (KRR) aimed at the same question.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors prove the precise asymptotic KRR test error at integer polynomial-regime thresholds, n/B(Ad,ℓ)→ψ. Double descent can occur depending on the effective regularization ζℓ and the effective SNRℓ, can recur at each integer κ (multiple descent), and can arise without label noise because high-degree target components act as effective noise.
record.recipe_differences: Uses asymptotic random-matrix and kernel-ridge-regression analysis on sphere or hypercube covariates, rather than deep-network model-size or epoch sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: Peak occurrence and peak size depend on the effective regularization and effective signal-to-noise ratio.

fits_no_version.finding: The paper characterizes the limiting Marchenko-Pastur spectrum of Gegenbauer kernel matrices (Theorem 2, Figure 2). This is a spectral result, not a test-error result.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Kernel matrix spectra in the polynomial regime converge to a shifted, rescaled Marchenko-Pastur law.

record.problems: The main test-error convergence result is for a class of typical random target functions; the paper notes that pointwise convergence for fixed targets at ℓ ≥ 2 is left for future work. Peak occurrence is conditional on effective regularization or effective SNR, and the results are asymptotic rather than finite-sample estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying test-error results left out. Figure 3 shows theoretical curves for selected effective-regularization values but does not provide extractable numeric values; its qualitative description is captured in r1.

untested.parts: Deep-network test error as model size grows; no neural network is trained.
Test error over training epochs; KRR is solved in closed form.
Deep-network training-set-size sweeps; only asymptotic KRR in sphere/hypercube settings is covered.
Model classes other than inner-product KRR (and its Gaussian-equivalent linear model).
No single effective-complexity measure predicting peak location across size, epochs and samples.
Whether optimally tuned ridge regularization eliminates the peak; the paper only shows that large ζ suppresses it.
No re-counting of effective parameters that turns the second descent into a U-shape.

missing.what: Dependence of peak height on effective regularization ζ. The peak increases as ζ decreases, and curves with large ζ (e.g., ζ=1.2, 2.0) show no peak. This bears on V6's claim that regularization removes the peak.
missing.locator: Section 1.1.2 discussion of V(ψ,ζ); Section 4.1; Figure 3

missing.what: No peak occurs for non-integer κ, where KRR fits exactly a degree-⌊κ⌋ polynomial (staircase). Peaks arise only at integer κ. This gives the conditions under which the second peak appears.

record.verdict_notes: This is a purely theoretical paper with no empirical sweeps; Figures 1 and 3 are theoretical curves. Convergence holds in probability over a class of random target functions; the pointwise result for fixed targets with ℓ≥2 is left open. I dropped the reader's limits_scope label on V6 for r2: effective noise acting through the variance term is consistent with V6's 'label noise or variance' wording. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Deep-network test error as model size grows.
The result is for asymptotic KRR sample-size ratios, not a deep-network training-data sweep.
Tests a conditional double-descent result for inner-product KRR, not a range of model classes or the full generality of the claim.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested across model size, epochs, and sample size.
The paper does not test whether optimally tuned regularization eliminates the peak.
No re-counting of complexity is used to turn a second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.subject: kernel ridge regression (KRR) with inner-product kernel
rows.operation_detail: Derives asymptotic test error as the sample-size ratio n/B(Ad, ℓ) tends to ψ.

conditions.value: uniform on the sphere or hypercube
typical random target functions satisfying Assumptions 2 and 3
a double descent can occur if ζℓ or effective SNRℓ is sufficiently small

rows.value: Fℓ²·B(ψ, ζ*) + (F>ℓ² + σε²)·V(ψ, ζ*) + F>ℓ² + o_d,P(1); the bias term decreases with ψ and the variance term peaks at ψ = 1. The total test error can show double descent under the stated small-regularization or low-effective-SNR condition.
rows.uncertainty: o_d,P(1); convergence in probability as d → ∞
rows.locator: Theorem 3, Eq. (19); discussion in Sections 1.1.2 and 4.1; Figure 3
rows.note: This is an asymptotic theoretical result, not a finite-sample empirical sweep.
rows.check: Links and state are correct, but the double descent is conditional: it appears only when effective regularization ζℓ or effective SNRℓ is small. The axis is the sample/dimension ratio ψ=n/B, not model size directly. V4's capacity reading relies on ψ<1 being the overparameterized side.

rows.subject: kernel ridge regression (KRR) with inner-product kernel
rows.operation_detail: Analyzes the asymptotic test-error contribution at polynomial degree ℓ when label noise is set to zero.

conditions.value: uniform on the sphere or hypercube
the high-degree target component P>ℓ f* can act as effective noise
a double descent can occur when effective regularization or effective SNR is sufficiently small

rows.value: The paper states that double descent can occur even when εi = 0; the high-degree target component can supply effective noise.
rows.note: The paper distinguishes this effective-noise bias-variance decomposition from the classical decomposition using label noise.
rows.check: The state is correct. The reader treated this as a qualification of V6, but V6 names 'label noise or variance' as the driver. The effective noise P>ℓ f* enters through the variance term, which is consistent with V6 rather than limiting it.

rows.subject: kernel ridge regression (KRR) with inner-product kernel
rows.operation_detail: Combines the polynomial-regime risk characterization across integer degree thresholds to describe multiple descent.

conditions.value: uniform on the sphere or hypercube
n = Θd(dκ), with integer thresholds κ = ℓ
peak at κ = ℓ can occur depending on effective regularization ζℓ and effective SNRℓ

rows.measure: Asymptotic test/prediction error across polynomial-regime thresholds
rows.value: A peak can occur each time κ crosses an integer; the resulting risk curve can have multiple descents and peaks of different sizes.
rows.note: The paper presents this as a theoretical explanation of multiple-descent behavior; it does not report a new numerical experiment for this result.
rows.check: Multiple peaks at each integer κ, of different sizes, bear directly on V6's multiple-descent clause. The row also bears on V4, since it describes the kernel risk curve as non-monotonic. The figure is a cartoon illustration, not computed values.

relationships.condition: Inner-product KRR, n/B(Ad,ℓ)→ψ near 1, small effective regularization ζℓ or small SNRℓ
relationships.reason: The variance term peaks at ψ=1, so adding samples just below the threshold raises asymptotic test error (r1).
relationships.display_finding: The variance term peaked at ψ = 1, increasing asymptotic test error as samples approached the threshold from below.

relationships.condition: Inner-product KRR on sphere/hypercube data under Assumptions 1–3, typical random targets
relationships.reason: The derived risk curve shows a peak at ψ=1 and falls again past it, in a non-deep model class (r1, r3).
relationships.display_finding: The derived risk curve peaked at ψ=1 and declined beyond it.

relationships.condition: Inner-product KRR in the polynomial regime
relationships.reason: The peak comes from the variance term, and the high-degree target component acts as effective noise even without label noise (r1, r2). Peaks recur at integer κ as multiple descent (r3).
relationships.display_finding: Variance generated the peak, with high-degree target components acting as effective noise without label noise, and peaks recurring at integer κ.
